The **Narval-class submarines** were a series of diesel-electric attack submarines built for the **French Navy** in the late 1950s and early 1960s. They were among the first post-WWII submarines designed in France and represented a significant step in the modernization of the French submarine fleet. Below is a detailed overview of the class: --- ### **1. Background & Development** - **Purpose**: The Narval-class was designed to replace older submarines from WWII (such as the *Saphir*-class) and to serve as **ocean-going attack submarines** capable of long-range patrols. - **Design Influence**: The class was influenced by German Type XXI U-boats (via the French acquisition of U-2518, renamed *Roland Morillot*), which featured advanced streamlining and high underwater speed. - **Builder**: **DCNS (Direction des Constructions Navales, now Naval Group)** at **Cherbourg Naval Dockyard**. - **Construction Period**: 1951–1960 (commissioned between 1957 and 1960). --- ### **2. Technical Specifications** | **Category** | **Details** | |--------------------|------------| | **Displacement** | 1,635 tons (surfaced), 1,910 tons (submerged) | | **Length** | 78.4 m (257 ft 3 in) | | **Beam** | 7.8 m (25 ft 7 in) | | **Draft** | 5.2 m (17 ft 1 in) | | **Propulsion** | - 2 × **SEMT-Pielstick 12PA4-185** diesel engines (2,400 hp each)
- 2 × electric motors (2,500 hp total)
- 2 × shafts | | **Speed** | 16 knots (30 km/h) surfaced, 18 knots (33 km/h) submerged | | **Range** | 15,000 nmi (28,000 km) at 8 knots surfaced, 100 nmi (190 km) at 5 knots submerged | | **Test Depth** | 200 m (656 ft) | | **Complement** | 63 (8 officers, 55 enlisted) | | **Armament** | - 8 × **550 mm (21.7 in) torpedo tubes** (6 bow, 2 stern)
- 14 × **L3 or L5 torpedoes** (or 32 mines)
- Later modified to carry **SM39 Exocet anti-ship missiles** (on *Dauphin* and *Marsouin*) | | **Sensors** | - **DUUA 1B** active/passive sonar
- **DRUA 31** radar
- **ARUR 10** electronic warfare suite | --- ### **3. Ships in the Class** Six submarines were built, all named after marine animals: | **Name** | **Pennant** | **Laid Down** | **Launched** | **Commissioned** | **Decommissioned** | **Fate** | |----------------|------------|--------------|-------------|------------------|--------------------|----------| | *Narval* (S631) | S631 | 1951 | 1954 | 1957 | 1983 | Scrapped 1986 | | *Marsouin* (S632) | S632 | 1952 | 1955 | 1957 | 1982 | Scrapped 1986 | | *Dauphin* (S633) | S633 | 1952 | 1955 | 1958 | 1992 | Museum ship (since 1996) | | *Requin* (S634) | S634 | 1953 | 1955 | 1958 | 1985 | Scrapped 1996 | | *Espadon* (S637) | S637 | 1955 | 1958 | 1960 | 1985 | Museum ship (since 1987) | | *Morse* (S638) | S638 | 1956 | 1958 | 1960 | 1986 | Scrapped 1992 | **Note**: - *Dauphin* and *Espadon* were preserved as **museum ships** (*Dauphin* in Saint-Nazaire, *Espadon* in Saint-Nazaire). - *Narval* was the lead ship and gave the class its name. --- ### **4. Operational History** - **Cold War Role**: The Narval-class served during the **Cold War**, conducting surveillance, intelligence-gathering, and anti-submarine warfare (ASW) missions. - **Modernizations**: - In the **1970s**, *Dauphin* and *Marsouin* were fitted with **SM39 Exocet anti-ship missiles**, making them the first French submarines capable of launching missiles. - Upgraded sonar and electronic warfare systems were installed over time. - **Exercises & Deployments**: - Participated in NATO exercises. - Conducted patrols in the **Atlantic, Mediterranean, and Indian Ocean**. - **Decommissioning**: The class was gradually phased out in the **1980s–1990s** as the **Agosta-class** and later **Rubis-class (nuclear)** submarines entered service. --- ### **5. Design Features & Innovations** - **Hull Design**: - **Teardrop-shaped hull** (inspired by Type XXI) for improved hydrodynamics. - **Double-hull construction** for better survivability. - **Propulsion**: - **Diesel-electric** with high underwater speed (18 knots). - **Snorkel** for diesel operation while submerged. - **Armament**: - **8 torpedo tubes** (6 bow, 2 stern) – a large loadout for the era. - Later **Exocet missile capability** (a first for French submarines). - **Habitability**: - Improved living conditions compared to WWII submarines. - Air conditioning and better crew spaces. --- ### **6. Comparison with Other Submarines of the Era** | **Feature** | **Narval-class** | **US Tang-class** | **UK Porpoise-class** | **Soviet Foxtrot-class** | |-------------------|------------------|-------------------|-----------------------|--------------------------| | **Displacement** | 1,910 t (sub) | 2,700 t (sub) | 2,080 t (sub) | 2,475 t (sub) | | **Speed (sub)** | 18 knots | 16 knots | 17 knots | 15 knots | | **Torpedo Tubes** | 8 (6 bow, 2 stern)| 6 (bow) | 8 (6 bow, 2 stern) | 10 (6 bow, 4 stern) | | **Missile Capable** | Yes (later) | No | No | No | | **Range** | 15,000 nmi | 11,000 nmi | 9,000 nmi | 20,000 nmi | **Key Takeaways**: - The Narval-class was **faster submerged** than most contemporaries. - It had a **larger torpedo loadout** than US and UK submarines of the time. - The **Exocet missile upgrade** made it one of the most advanced diesel-electric submarines in the 1970s. --- ### **7. Legacy & Influence** - **First Post-War French Submarine**: The Narval-class set the foundation for later French submarine designs, including the **Daphné-class** and **Agosta-class**. - **Exocet Integration**: The missile upgrades on *Dauphin* and *Marsouin* paved the way for future French submarine-launched weapons. - **Museum Ships**: *Dauphin* and *Espadon* remain as **popular tourist attractions**, showcasing Cold War submarine technology. --- ### **8. Notable Incidents & Events** - **1961**: *Narval* participated in **Operation Trikora** (French support for Indonesia during the West New Guinea dispute). - **1970s**: *Dauphin* and *Marsouin* were **modified for Exocet missiles**, making them the first French submarines with anti-ship missile capability. - **1980s**: The class was gradually replaced by the **Agosta-class** (diesel-electric) and **Rubis-class** (nuclear attack submarines). --- ### **9. Where to See Them Today** - **S633 *Dauphin*** – **Saint-Nazaire Submarine Base (France)** (on display since 1996). - **S637 *Espadon*** – **Saint-Nazaire Submarine Base (France)** (on display since 1987). Both submarines are open to the public and offer a glimpse into **Cold War-era submarine technology**. --- ### **10. Further Reading & Sources** - **Books**: - *French Submarines of World War II* (John Jordan) - *Cold War Submarines: The Design and Construction of U.S. and Soviet Submarines* (Norman Polmar & K.J. Moore) - **Online Resources**: - [Naval Group (DCNS) Archives](https://www.naval-group.com/) - [French Navy Official Website](https://www.defense.gouv.fr/marine) - [Submarine Matters – Narval-class](https://www.submarinematters.com/) --- ### **Final Thoughts** The **Narval-class** was a **critical step in France’s post-war submarine development**, blending **German WWII innovations** with **French engineering**. While overshadowed by later nuclear submarines, they played a key role in **Cold War naval operations** and introduced **missile capability** to French submarines.
